To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sources of utilitarian value are: ease of use, convenience, and price; the inhibitors are: lack of privacy, lack of product knowledge, lack of product quality, and lack of trust; the sources of hedonic value are: enjoyment and entertainment; and the inhibitors are: privacy, and lack of product knowledge.

(1) Internet shopping situations can be classified on the basis of their fulfillment and product characteristics, and (2) the sources and inhibitors for utilitarian and hedonistic value vary across these categories.

the utilitarian value of Internet shopping is positively related to the degree of product customization, the hedonic value of Internet shopping positively relates to the level of product interactivity, and the utilitarian value is negatively related to the level of social interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the sources and inhibitors, of the utilitarian and hedonistic value, that are associated with each category of Internet Shopping?
the sources and inhibitors that influence the perceived utilitarian and hedonistic value of Internet shopping.
the question: What is the nature of utilitarian and/or hedonic value for Internet shopping in various product-fulfillment categories?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
utilitarian value is more strongly associated with the fulfillment of the utilitarian needs and hedonic value with the fulfillment of hedonic needs.
the sources of utilitarian value are similar across all categories of Internet shopping, while the sources of hedonic value are more varied.
the sources and inhibitors for utilitarian and hedonistic value are not the same across the Internet shopping categories that are identified in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while utilitarian value is the primary driver of overall satisfaction with Internet shopping, hedonic value also plays an important role, especially when the Internet shopping experience is not entirely utilitarian.

, while utilitarian value is generally a more significant driver of satisfaction than hedonic value, hedonic value is more likely to be a source of satisfaction when the Internet shopping situation is characterized as a'search' or 'information' product category.

utilitarian value is more strongly related to fulfillment characteristics than to product characteristics, and that hedonic value is more strongly influenced by product characteristics than fulfillment characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
utilitarian and hedonistic value are not necessarily the same across different types of online shopping activities.
the sources and inhibitors that are relevant for utilitarian value differ substantially from those for hedonic value.
the sources and inhibitors are not the same across all Internet shopping categories, and that the sources and/or inhibitors of hedonic value are often different from those for utilitarian value.
